publisher.title: Publisher
wiz.heading: Family Relay Publisher
wiz.intro: Stand up a server that produces routes for your trusted recipients. Seven steps, around 10 minutes for a fresh operator.
wiz.step.label: Step {n} of {total}
wiz.step.operator.title: Operator
wiz.step.operator.blurb: An operator is one server you publish from. Pick an existing one or create a new label so we can keep its keys, tokens and pricing scoped together.
wiz.step.provider.title: Provider & tokens
wiz.step.provider.blurb: Tell us which cloud you rent the relay from, and paste the API token for that account. Tokens are encrypted on disk with the PIN you also set here.
wiz.step.pricing.title: Region & sizing
wiz.step.pricing.blurb: Pick the region, server type and which transport families to enable on this operator. We look up live pricing so you know what monthly cost to expect.
wiz.step.keys.title: Publisher keys
wiz.step.keys.blurb: Generate a new Ed25519 signing key for this operator. Recipients trust your routes by recognising this key, so back up the fingerprint shown here.
wiz.step.provision.title: Provision
wiz.step.provision.blurb: Daal calls the cloud provider, spins up the server, hardens it and runs the toolbox bring-up. You can watch the live progress log.
wiz.step.sign.title: Sign relaypack
wiz.step.sign.blurb: We bundle the operator's endpoints into a signed relaypack (a .sbp file) that recipients import to gain a route. The publisher name and phase are written into that bundle.
wiz.step.distribute.title: Distribute
wiz.step.distribute.blurb: Hand the relaypack to recipients. Daal can render it as a QR fountain that any phone can scan, or save the .sbp file to disk so you can deliver it any way you like.

relaypack.p1: A RelayPack is a small set of internet routes your diaspora family member set up for you on a server outside Iran. Your Daal app picks the route that works best on your network right now. If one route stops working, Daal switches to another automatically.
relaypack.p2: They rented a small server (about €5/month) and ran a one-time wizard that sets the server up safely. The server is yours; nothing leaves their machine; nobody else uses your routes.
relaypack.h3: What does your Daal app do?
relaypack.p3: When your network changes — new Wi-Fi, mobile data, café — Daal runs five small probes to see what works on this network. It picks the best route from your RelayPack and explains its choice in one sentence. If a route fails, it cools down and tries another. No information leaves your phone.
